edges.description: Excess extracellular synaptic dopamine during early infancy drives chorea, ballismus, and orolingual dyskinesia prior to presynaptic depletion.
Dopaminergic neurotransmission dyshomeostasis produces episodic conjugate ocular deviation characteristic of monoamine transport defects.
Early infantile monoaminergic dysregulation manifests with nonspecific irritability before overt parkinsonism.
Early oromotor and bulbar dopaminergic dysfunction impairs infant feeding.
Early striatal dopaminergic imbalance produces truncal hypotonia in infancy.
Partial DAT deficiency and dysregulated synaptic dopamine clearance in atypical later-onset DTDS manifest as childhood ADHD prior to overt parkinsonism-dystonia.
Severe nigrostriatal dopaminergic failure and refractory generalized dystonia predispose to recurrent status dystonicus crises.
Progressive nigrostriatal dopaminergic failure and limitation of voluntary movement produce severe gross motor developmental delay.
Severe generalized dystonic exacerbations can escalate into recurrent status dystonicus crises.

nodes.description: For severe dystonia poorly controlled by dopamine agonists alone, GeneReviews lists trihexyphenidyl, baclofen, gabapentin, and clonidine as adjunctive agents, with chloral hydrate (alongside benzodiazepines) used acutely for dystonic exacerbations or status dystonicus.

evidence.snippet: adjuncts such as trihexyphenidyl, baclofen, gabapentin, and clonidine for severe dystonia; and chloral hydrate and benzodiazepines for exacerbations of dystonia or status dystonicus.

nodes.description: In atypical later-onset DTDS, childhood attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) after normal early psychomotor development precedes later manifestations of parkinsonism-dystonia and tremor.

evidence.snippet: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is reported in childhood followed by later-onset manifestations of parkinsonism-dystonia with tremor, progressive bradykinesia, variable tone, and dystonic posturing.

nodes.description: Axial (truncal) hypotonia is among the early nonspecific infantile findings in classic early-onset DTDS.

evidence.snippet: Infants typically manifest nonspecific findings (irritability, feeding difficulties, axial hypotonia, and/or delayed motor development)

nodes.description: Benzodiazepines are used to control chorea and dyskinesia in early disease and for exacerbations of dystonia or status dystonicus.

evidence.snippet: chloral hydrate and benzodiazepines for exacerbations of dystonia or status dystonicus.

nodes.description: Bradykinesia is a core parkinsonian feature that progresses to akinesia, with limitation of voluntary movements leading to severe motor delay.

evidence.snippet: affected individuals develop parkinsonism-dystonia characterized by bradykinesia (progressing to akinesia), dystonic posturing, distal tremor, rigidity, and reduced facial expression.

nodes.description: Reduced facial expression (hypomimia) accompanies the parkinsonian phase.

evidence.snippet: bradykinesia (progressing to akinesia), dystonic posturing, distal tremor, rigidity, and reduced facial expression.

nodes.description: Delayed motor development is an early feature in classic early-onset DTDS; limitation of voluntary movements later leads to severe motor delay.

evidence.snippet: Infants typically manifest nonspecific findings (irritability, feeding difficulties, axial hypotonia, and/or delayed motor development)

nodes.description: Dopamine agonists pramipexole and ropinirole are used as first-line agents for dystonia, which is more difficult to control than chorea. The older ergot dopamine agonists bromocriptine and pergolide are generally avoided because of fibrosis risk.

evidence.snippet: Dystonia is more difficult to control, and treatment often includes the dopamine agonists pramipexole and ropinirole as first-line agents

Although the dopamine agonists bromocriptine and pergolide could be considered, the associated increased risk of pulmonary, retroperitoneal, and pericardial fibrosis makes them less desirable than the newer dopamine agonists.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC6A3 produce a mutant dopamine transporter (DAT) with multifaceted dysfunction: reduced transporter activity, impaired dopamine binding, reduced cell-surface expression, and aberrant posttranslational modification with impaired glycosylation. The net effect is a profound deficit in presynaptic reuptake of dopamine from the synaptic cleft.

evidence.reference_title: Dopamine Transporter Deficiency Syndrome (DTDS): Expanding the Clinical Phenotype and Precision Medicine Approaches.
evidence.snippet: Amino acid substitutions result in mutant proteins with impaired dopamine transporter function due to reduced transporter activity, impaired dopamine binding, reduced cell-surface expression, and aberrant posttranslational protein modification with impaired glycosylation.

evidence.reference_title: Psychomotor impairments and therapeutic implications revealed by a mutation associated with infantile Parkinsonism-Dystonia.
evidence.snippet: Common to DTDS-linked DAT variants is a multifaceted loss of DAT function, which includes impaired transporter activity and decreased expression

nodes.description: Excess synaptic dopamine and impaired handling lead to dopamine toxicity, oxidative/carbonyl stress, TNF-alpha-mediated inflammation, and apoptotic neurodegeneration of midbrain dopaminergic neurons, demonstrated in patient iPSC-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons and in the DAT knockout mouse, which recapitulates tremor, bradykinesia, and premature death. Direct human DTDS neuropathology has not yet been reported (see HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion). The substantia nigra and striatum are the principal affected structures of the nigrostriatal system, and their dysfunction underlies the progressive parkinsonism-dystonia phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Gene therapy restores dopamine transporter expression and ameliorates pathology in iPSC and mouse models of infantile parkinsonism.
evidence.snippet: we generated a midbrain dopaminergic (mDA) neuron model of DTDS that exhibited marked impairment of DAT activity, apoptotic neurodegeneration associated with TNFα-mediated inflammation, and dopamine toxicity.

evidence.reference_title: Gene therapy restores dopamine transporter expression and ameliorates pathology in iPSC and mouse models of infantile parkinsonism.
evidence.snippet: we used the knockout mouse model of DTDS that recapitulates human disease, exhibiting parkinsonism features, including tremor, bradykinesia, and premature death.

nodes.description: Impaired DAT-mediated reuptake reduces dopamine clearance, raising extracellular synaptic dopamine and increasing dopamine turnover. This is reflected biochemically as elevated cerebrospinal fluid homovanillic acid (HVA, a dopamine catabolite) with normal 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA), yielding a raised HVA:5-HIAA ratio, and clinically by abnormal striatal dopamine transporter (DAT) SPECT imaging.

evidence.reference_title: Gene therapy restores dopamine transporter expression and ameliorates pathology in iPSC and mouse models of infantile parkinsonism.
evidence.snippet: Patients present with early infantile hyperkinesia, severe progressive childhood parkinsonism, and raised cerebrospinal fluid dopamine metabolites.

evidence.reference_title: Psychomotor impairments and therapeutic implications revealed by a mutation associated with infantile Parkinsonism-Dystonia.
evidence.snippet: Increased levels of HVA might reflect increased DA turnover promoted by higher extracellular DA levels.

evidence.reference_title: Dopamine transporter deficiency syndrome: phenotypic spectrum from infancy to adulthood.
evidence.snippet: We advocate that in adolescents or adults with a clinical picture of juvenile parkinsonism (onset <20 years) investigations for DTDS should be considered, including: (i) CSF neurotransmitter studies; (ii) DAT SPECT scan (abnormal in DTDS) ( Kurian et al., 2011a ); and (iii) SLC6A3 sequencing.

nodes.description: Dystonia with dystonic posturing is a hallmark feature across classic and atypical DTDS; it is difficult to control and may escalate into episodic status dystonicus.

evidence.snippet: Episodic status dystonicus, exacerbations of dystonia, and secondary orthopedic, gastrointestinal, and respiratory complications are common.

nodes.description: Feeding difficulties are among the early nonspecific infantile findings in classic DTDS and progress with bulbar dysfunction, frequently requiring artificial enteral nutrition via nasogastric or gastrostomy tube.

evidence.snippet: Infants typically manifest nonspecific findings (irritability, feeding difficulties, axial hypotonia, and/or delayed motor development)

evidence.reference_title: Dopamine transporter deficiency syndrome: phenotypic spectrum from infancy to adulthood.
evidence.snippet: All patients developed bulbar dysfunction and required artificial feeding through the nasogastric/gastrostomy route.

nodes.description: Focal intramuscular botulinum toxin injections are used to manage severe focal hypertonia and reduce secondary orthopedic contractures.

evidence.snippet: medical management of tone issues and regular physical therapy to reduce the risk of contractures and fractures; focal botulinum toxin for contractures

nodes.description: AAV- and lentivirus-mediated gene therapy delivering wild-type SLC6A3 is in preclinical development. In patient iPSC-derived neurons and DAT knockout mice, SLC6A3 gene transfer restored DAT activity, prevented neurodegeneration, and improved motor phenotype and survival; targeted midbrain delivery avoided off-target toxicity. This approach is investigational and not yet an approved therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Gene therapy restores dopamine transporter expression and ameliorates pathology in iPSC and mouse models of infantile parkinsonism.
evidence.snippet: These were avoided with stereotactic delivery of AAV2.SLC6A3 gene therapy targeted to the midbrain of adult knockout mice, which rescued both motor phenotype and neurodegeneration, suggesting that targeted AAV gene therapy might be effective for patients with DTDS.

evidence.reference_title: Gene Therapy for Dopamine Dyshomeostasis: From Parkinson's to Primary Neurotransmitter Diseases.
evidence.snippet: Here, we review recent advances in gene therapy, focused on the targeted delivery of dopaminergic genes for Parkinson's disease and the primary neurotransmitter disorders, AADC deficiency and dopamine transporter deficiency syndrome (DTDS).

evidence.snippet: followed by a hyperkinetic movement disorder (with features of chorea, dystonia, ballismus, orolingual dyskinesia).

nodes.description: Oculogyric crises (episodic conjugate upward deviation of the eyes) are a characteristic eye-movement feature reported in infantile parkinsonism-dystonia and related monoamine neurotransmitter disorders.

evidence.snippet: Two cases had eye movement abnormalities with saccadic intrusion on smooth pursuit in one and recurrent oculogyric crises in the other.

evidence.reference_title: Dopamine transporter deficiency syndrome: phenotypic spectrum from infancy to adulthood.
evidence.snippet: The eye movement abnormalities of DTDS include oculogyric crises, ocular flutter and saccade initiation failure ( Kurian et al., 2011a ).

evidence.reference_title: Dopamine Transporter Deficiency Syndrome (DTDS): Expanding the Clinical Phenotype and Precision Medicine Approaches.
evidence.snippet: Infantile parkinsonism-dystonia due to dopamine transporter deficiency syndrome (DTDS) is an ultrarare childhood movement disorder caused by biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the SLC6A3 gene.
In most individuals reported to date, SLC6A3-related DTDS is caused by biallelic loss-of-function pathogenic variants and inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.
Autosomal dominant SLC6A3-related DTDS caused by a heterozygous dominant-negative SLC6A3 pathogenic variant has been reported in one individual to date.

nodes.description: Episodic status dystonicus (paroxysmal dystonic storm) is a common, life-threatening emergency manifestation of generalized dystonia in DTDS requiring acute intervention with benzodiazepines or chloral hydrate.

evidence.snippet: Episodic status dystonicus, exacerbations of dystonia, and secondary orthopedic, gastrointestinal, and respiratory complications are common.

evidence.reference_title: Dopamine transporter deficiency syndrome: phenotypic spectrum from infancy to adulthood.
evidence.snippet: Two children developed chorea of their lower limbs and had paroxysmal dystonic storms.

nodes.description: Standard pharmacotherapy has limited efficacy in DTDS. Supportive management includes nutrition and feeding support, physical therapy to reduce contracture and fracture risk, management of respiratory infections, and treatment of pain that can exacerbate movement disorders. Care is largely supportive given the absence of disease-modifying therapy.

evidence.snippet: Supportive management and developmental support includes: nutrition management and feeding support for oral feeding issues

nodes.description: Tetrabenazine, a vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2) inhibitor, is used to control chorea and dyskinesia in the early hyperkinetic stages of disease.

evidence.snippet: Treatment to control chorea and dyskinesia in early stages of the disease includes tetrabenazine and benzodiazepines.

nodes.description: Distal and dystonic tremor (involving limbs, head, or tongue) is a feature of both classic and atypical later-onset DTDS.
